### **Recursive Definition**

$$

\begin{cases} 
5 & \text{if } n = 1, \\
2 \cdot f\left(\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor\right) & \text{if } n \text{ is even}, \\
2 \cdot f\left(\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor\right) + 1 & \text{if } n \text{ is odd and } n > 1.
\end{cases}
$$

---

### **Explanation**

- **Base Case**: When `n = 1`, the value is `5`, which is the root of the tree.
- **Recursive Case**:
  - If `n` is **even**, it is the **left child** of the node at position `n // 2`, so we compute `2 * f(n // 2)`.
  - If `n` is **odd**, it is the **right child** of the node at position `n // 2`, so we compute `2 * f(n // 2) + 1`.

This recursive structure mirrors the binary heap indexing, where each node at position `i` has left and right children at positions `2i` and `2i + 1`, respectively.

```python
def f(n):

        return 5
    parent = n // 2
    if n % 2 == 0:
        return 2 * f(parent)
    else:
        return 2 * f(parent) + 1
```
